_doc: Single source of every timing, level and layout number. Edit here, then run `python3 -I scripts/numbers_gen.py` — it rewrites references/craft/numbers.md and assets/remotion-template/src/numbers.ts. Python scripts read it through scripts/common.py (N[key]). Frames are at 30 fps on the 1080x1920 canvas (Reel2K scales by 4/3).

rows.what: dissolve on every timeline cut (frames)
rows.why: the outgoing clip is held muted under the incoming one

rows.what: board / b-roll fade in and out (frames)
rows.why: crossfade between boards; the timeline dissolve is a different thing

rows.what: a cutaway or board over a cut starts at least this many frames before the cut
rows.why: the outgoing face must not peek out

rows.what: … and ends at least this many frames after it
rows.why: xfade 7 + layerFade 12: its fade-out must start after the incoming shot's own dissolve, less shows a stray face or the dark carrier

rows.what: hard cuts inside a montage: next shot starts this many frames before the previous ends (with fadeIn/fadeOut 0)
rows.why: no dip to the carrier between shots

rows.what: flash on a chapter cut, peak opacity
rows.why: 0.85 read as a strobe

sections.title: Audio levels (Remotion volume; the render then sets the whole mix to the target with a static gain)

rows.what: final integrated loudness (LUFS)
render fails if the final file is further off the target than this (LU)
rows.why: an auto-levelling limiter once shipped every reel at −14.9

rows.what: music bed under speech
rows.why: ≈ 20 LU down

rows.what: bed in the cold open, wordless pauses and the tail
bed length = cut list totalFrames / 30 + this (s)
rows.why: covers the end card and the fade

rows.what: whoosh on a chapter tag
soft whoosh on a scan or slide (0.12–0.16)
done.wav when a result lands (0.2–0.24)
pop.wav on a chip, badge or mark (0.18–0.22)
tick.wav while a number counts (0.3–0.35; 0.5 only for a lone timer)
tick spacing while counting (frames)
soft bleep peak (dBFS)
rows.why: −16 read as loud

rows.what: length of one Sfx sequence (frames)
rows.why: long enough for the decay of every sound in audio/sfx

rows.what: frames the bed takes to move between bedUnder and bedOpen
rows.why: a jump in the bed level is heard as a cut

rows.what: bed fade at the very end of the reel (frames)
impact on the drop / a punch (action reel)
rows.why: the one sound that marks the big moment; everything else is the track's

rows.what: camera shutter (a photo moment, a freeze)
tape rewind (a replay, a «back to…» cut)
rising noise into a drop or a reveal (0.9 s, ends on the frame it is placed + 27)
short electronic beep (a low battery, a warning)
falling tone (the camera dies, the end)
a real recorded sound from sfx_find.py (Openverse), normalised to −20 LUFS — R.sfx(at, "real_<name>")
rows.why: about as loud as the designed pops and whooshes at their levels

rows.what: variants made of every whoosh / pop / hit (whoosh, whoosh2, whoosh3 …); reelgen.sfx cycles them
rows.why: «одинаковый вжух на каждый переход — странно» (Halloween reel): the same sample twice in a row reads as a template

smallest text on screen

rows.what: x264 CRF of the proxies
--trim-to-cutlist pad on each side of the used range (s)
rows.why: room for dissolves and small re-cuts without re-encoding

rows.what: Remotion frame JPEG quality
rows.why: 80 bands dark gradients

rows.what: frames per second people_zones.py samples from the source
rows.why: a person crossing the frame in ~1 s is seen 4 times; 10 s of 4K scan in ≈ 3 s

rows.what: lowest Vision confidence for a person box
rows.why: lower picks up posters and dark shapes

rows.what: share of the crop width the chosen people may fill
rows.why: a person touching both crop edges looks cut off

rows.what: a second person joins the crop only if their box is ≥ this share of the main one
rows.why: small background crowd must not pull the crop away from the subject

rows.what: the crop keeps its person while they are at least this share of the biggest one
rows.why: a standing and a crouching person swap «biggest» every few frames; without stickiness the crop swings between them

rows.what: smoothing window of the per-frame crop centre (s)
rows.why: one missed or wrong detection must not jerk the crop

rows.what: subject movement (share of the frame width) below which the crop is one fixed centre
rows.why: a still shot that wobbles a few pixels reads as a shaky camera

rows.what: fastest crop pan (frame widths per second)
rows.why: following a quick move faster than this looks like a glitch

rows.what: seconds between crop keyframes of a panning segment
rows.why: enough to follow a walk, few enough for one ffmpeg expression per proxy

rows.what: a range that starts inside a sentence grows back to its start, at most this many seconds
rows.why: Halloween vlog v2: «фразы обрезанные посередине» — a line that starts mid-thought reads as a mistake

rows.what: a range that ends inside a sentence grows forward to its end, at most this many seconds
rows.why: same; forward is shorter — the punchline is usually already in

rows.what: a pause at least this long counts as a sentence edge even without .?!… (s)
rows.why: Parakeet / Whisper often drop the full stop of spoken Russian

rows.what: ranges of one take further apart than this get their own alias proxy (s)
rows.why: make_proxies encodes one window per clip: c0080 was 509 s of 4K for 70 s used

sections.title: Voice chain (voice_clean.py restores each source → dialogue.py builds and processes one dialogue stem → render.sh masters)

rows.what: DeepFilterNet noise reduction limit per lav channel (dB)
rows.why: full strength left a hollow «из толчка» voice (A/B by ear, Halloween vlog)

rows.what: automix exponent: channel gain ∝ power^(this/2) share
rows.why: pushes the far mic's late copy of a voice down (comb filtering)

rows.what: active speech level of every clip before the render's static gain (dBFS)
rows.why: clips varied by up to 25 dB between cameras and mics

rows.what: most a quiet clip is lifted (dB)
rows.why: +18 dB lifted mic hiss and DeepFilterNet artefacts into «a speaker about to blow»

rows.what: a speech segment quieter than this is lifted (dBFS)
rows.why: a whisper inside a loud clip

rows.what: a speech segment louder than this is lowered (dBFS)
rows.why: a shout inside a calm clip

rows.what: most a single segment is moved (dB)
rows.why: ±10 dB per segment pumped the noise floor

rows.what: camera sound under a picture beat ("amb"), active level (dBFS)
rows.why: a dance or a ride in digital silence feels dead in a vlog without music

rows.what: camera sound instead of the voice ("raw") (dBFS)
rows.why: DeepFilterNet swallowed a voice inside a costume

rows.what: samples at |x| ≥ 0.985 before a source counts as clipped and gets adeclip
rows.why: adeclip on clean audio still rewrote the samples (diff up to −34 dBFS, 2026-11-07 audit)

rows.what: how far under the speech the residual noise should sit after cleanup (dB); DeepFilterNet's limit = this − the source SNR
rows.why: full-strength DeepFilterNet turned every pause into digital silence (−69 dB) and cut −3 dB at 3.15 kHz out of the voice; a floor ≈ 48 dB down is inaudible under −16 LUFS speech and keeps the pauses natural

rows.what: smallest DeepFilterNet limit used (dB); a source with SNR ≥ noiseTargetDb skips DeepFilterNet
rows.why: a quiet room needs no neural cleanup — every pass costs some timbre

rows.what: largest DeepFilterNet limit (dB)
rows.why: more than ≈ 18 dB pumps the noise between words and hollows the voice («из толчка», «underwater»)

rows.what: equal-power crossfade on every jump cut of the dialogue (ms, centred on the cut, from source handles)
rows.why: a hard switch of the waveform clicks; 2–10 ms is the dialogue-editing norm, longer smears consonants

rows.what: linear crossfade where two segments continue the same take (a gain change, not a cut)
high-pass of the voice (12 dB/oct)
rows.why: rumble, wind and lav handling noise live under the voice's fundamental (85–180 Hz)

rows.what: centre of the phase rotator (4 all-pass sections, Q 0.7) after the high-pass
rows.why: speech waveforms are lopsided (+0.92 / −0.71 on the 2026-11-05 reel): rotating the phase lowers the peaks ≈ 2.5 dB without changing the spectrum (broadcast voice processing), so the limiter works less

rows.what: share of the measured deviation from the target speech spectrum that the tonal EQ corrects
rows.why: a partial match keeps the speaker's own timbre

rows.what: deepest mud (315 Hz) / box (900 Hz) cut (dB)
largest presence boost at 3.5 kHz (dB)
rows.why: the DJI lav under clothing sat ~20 dB down at 2–5 kHz vs its 400–500 Hz peak: dull, «muffled»

rows.what: largest air boost (9 kHz shelf, dB)
rows.why: more lifts the lav's hiss and the AAC artefacts of the camera track

rows.what: the one compressor's threshold over the leveled speech (dB over voiceTargetDb)
rows.why: three compressors/limiters in a row squeezed LRA from 8.5 to 2.6 LU; +2 dB / 2.5:1 on 10 ms frames still gave 3.9 LU on the 2026-11-05 reel, +4 / 2:1 / 30 ms gives 5.0

rows.what: its ratio
its soft knee (dB)
its attack (ms)
its release (ms)
its RMS detector window (ms)
rows.why: 10 ms frames compressed inside syllables

rows.what: de-esser acts where the 6.5 kHz band is louder than the speech level + this (dB) and dominates the frame
rows.why: a dark lav needs none; a bright one gets 2–4 dB on each «с/ш»

rows.what: deepest de-esser cut (dB)
integrated loudness of the finished dialogue stem (reel/public/audio/dialogue.wav)
rows.why: the music bed and SFX levels were tuned against speech at about this level; render.sh lifts the whole mix to targetLufs

rows.what: look-ahead peak ceiling of the stem (dBFS)
rows.why: speech off a lav peaks 18–23 dB over its loudness; at −12 the limiter worked 31–66 % of the time (audible), at −10 ≈ 12 % with ≤ 5 dB on the rare peaks; render.sh adds ≈ +8 dB and its true-peak limiter catches the rest

rows.what: master true-peak ceiling (dBTP; 4× oversampled limiter in render.sh)
rows.why: sample-peak limiting let inter-sample peaks through; AAC adds ≈ 0.5 dB more

rows.what: final AAC bitrate (the only lossy encode of the sound; Remotion renders PCM)
rows.why: proxies 192k → Remotion 320k → final 192k = three extra generations on top of the camera's AAC

rows.what: audio_qa warns above this loudness range of the final mix (LU)
audio_qa warns below this (LU): over-compressed
rows.why: the 2026-11-05 reel shipped at 2.6 LU

rows.what: mean luma (0–255) below which a clip gets the strong shadow lift
rows.why: night street clips came out of the LUT almost black on a phone

rows.what: … the medium lift
rows.why: bar and porch clips: faces in the mud

rows.what: … the mild lift; brighter clips are untouched
rows.why: a global grade washed out the day clips

rows.what: a piece slower than this is retimed with motion-compensated interpolation (minterpolate)
rows.why: the browser only repeats frames: 40 % slow motion of a 25 fps clip stuttered

rows.what: bars per musical phrase on the reel grid (whips and big moments go on phrase starts)
rows.why: Cudi «Pursuit Of Happiness (Nightmare)»: sections every 4 bars from the drop (frames 218/468/718/967/1217)

rows.what: longest entrance of one element (frames); a longer build is a stagger of several elements
rows.why: HyperFrames motion doctrine (2026-11-08): a single slow element reads as lag

rows.what: total stagger of one group of items (first start → last start)
rows.why: a longer cascade makes the viewer wait for the last item

rows.what: an exit lasts this share of the matching entrance
rows.why: leaving is faster than arriving; the eye has already read it

rows.what: shortest still beat between an action and its result (frames)
rows.why: the dramatic comma: count-up ends → hold → the stamp lands; straight to the result loses it

rows.what: longest still beat before a payoff (frames)
rows.why: longer reads as a stall

rows.what: kinds of scene transition in one reel (dissolve, hand-off, whip …), repeated
rows.why: a new transition per chapter reads as a template showcase

rows.what: effect seams (anything but a dissolve / hard cut) per minute of a calm reel, at most
rows.why: the user, 2026-11-09: «вжух на каждое действие» makes a terrible video — most cuts stay plain

rows.what: plain cuts between two effect seams, at least (calm reel)
rows.why: alternation: an effect only reads against plain cuts around it

rows.what: plain shots between two effect moments in an action reel (whip, crash, rgb, stutter, bump), at least — the drop and phrase starts excepted
rows.why: same rule at action tempo

rows.what: the same seam kind does not come back within this many seconds
rows.why: a repeated trick turns into a template

rows.what: push seam: frames the outgoing clip accelerates into the zoom before the cut
rows.why: video-shotcraft crash-zoom card: over 10 f it reads as an ordinary push

rows.what: push seam: outgoing scale multiplier at the cut
rows.why: enough to read as a move, the zoom blur hides the jump

rows.what: push seam: frames the incoming clip keeps pushing in while the blur clears
rows.why: the camera keeps the same direction across the cut (motion-design.md «sign of a zoom»)

rows.what: push seam: incoming scale growth over seamPushIn
rows.why: forward momentum that settles

rows.what: push seam: radial zoom blur at the cut (px, @remotion/effects zoomBlur)
rows.why: tested on a 2K proxy 2026-11-09: 40–50 hides the cut, 70+ smears the face

rows.what: blur seam: frames the outgoing clip defocuses before the cut
rows.why: motionmaxxing blur-matched cut: 3–8 f ramp

rows.what: blur seam: frames the incoming clip resolves
blur seam: defocus at the cut (px on the 1080 canvas)
rows.why: both sides meet at the same blur

rows.what: leak seam: frames the warm light builds before the cut (ease-in)
rows.why: hidden cut through a light leak, slower in than out

rows.what: leak seam: frames the light clears after the cut (ease-out)
leak seam: peak opacity of the warm gradients
rows.why: the user: no super-bright transitions — @remotion/effects lightLeak fills the frame solid yellow at its peak, not used

rows.what: leak seam: brightness lift of the picture at the peak
rows.why: with contrast −20 %, saturation −15 % it reads as light, not a white flash

rows.what: wipe seam: frames of a soft wipe in the reel's current (right → left)
wipe seam: soft edge width (share of the canvas width)
rows.why: a hard edge looks like a slideshow

rows.what: match seam: frames the incoming clip eases from the matched framing back to its own
rows.why: the head lands where the previous head was, then the frame settles

rows.what: match seam: largest zoom used to line the heads up (beyond it → a plain dissolve, WARNING)
rows.why: 2K proxies soften beyond ≈ 1.5

rows.what: action shake amplitude at the hit (px)
rows.why: video-shotcraft: > 20 px reads as a glitch; was 22 px linear

rows.what: action shake decay constant (frames, e^(−t/τ)); gone in ≈ 6 f
action RGB split at its peak (px on the 1080 canvas)
rows.why: short and on a hit only; a constant split reads as a broken screen

rows.what: action RGB split length (frames)
RGB splits per reel, at most
bump cut: the shot pushes in by this much over bumpFrames on the beat
rows.why: Remotion pushCut idea: a hard cut with a scale pulse

rows.what: bump cut length (frames)
bump cut: white flash peak (2 frames); 0 = none
rows.why: ≤ 0.2: a hint, not a strobe

rows.what: crash zooms per reel, at most
full-frame impacts (flash ≥ 0.3 or shake) per reel, at most
rows.why: video-shotcraft beat-sync: 3 hits, ≥ 16 beats apart

rows.what: beats between two full-frame impacts, at least
stutter into a drop: the picture advances every N frames
rows.why: each step must move visibly or it reads as dropped frames

rows.what: L-cut: seconds the outgoing scene's own sound carries under the next picture (scene changes, bridge option)
rows.why: OpenMontage edit-director: 0.5–1.5 s on the hardest seams

rows.what: J-cut: seconds the incoming scene's own sound starts before its picture
